coordinates.note: Surface building serving the underground hall; the hall itself sits below at an offset no fetched source publishes, hence the precision.

name: ECN3 cavern, CERN North Area
notes: facility:cern is owned by the cern-atlas workstream; this record only references it.

Coordinates are the CERN Prevessin campus point, at the same precision and for the same reason as the existing site:cern-neutrino-platform-ehn1 record: no fetched source gives a surveyed point for this specific cavern.
Shared by experiment:na48, experiment:na62 and (planned) experiment:ship.

2026-09-17 fixed-target verification: `coordinates.kind` was `detector`, which is dishonest under A23 (a campus-grade point relabelled `detector` to satisfy the validator, which then passes silently instead of emitting the honest `coordinate-kind-approximate` warning). Corrected to `campus`, matching this record's own note that the point is campus precision, not hall/cavern precision.

summary.plain: An underground cavern in CERN's North Area, on the French side of the laboratory, that has held a succession of kaon-decay experiments: NA48, then NA62, and reserved for the future SHiP experiment.
summary.technical: ECN3 underground cavern (with its TCC8 target/beam area) in the CERN SPS North Area on the Prevessin site, fed by the P42 and K12 beamlines; successive home of NA48 (1997-2001), NA62 (2015-present) and the planned SHiP experiment.
